change: Additive approval-batch schema on the existing Host database (MissionStore)

tables.name: approval_batches

columns.actions: TEXT NOT NULL (JSON array, exact action ids, no wildcards)
columns.target_json: TEXT NOT NULL (JSON {app, processId, title}; processId null allowed)
columns.record: TEXT NOT NULL (full ApprovalBatch JSON; the used_count column and record.usedCount are rewritten together in the admission UPDATE, so reads can never see divergent counts)

indexes: CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_approval_batches_mission ON approval_batches(mission_id)

permission_requests: NO new column: the batch offer lives inside the permission_requests `record` JSON (PermissionBatchOffer on PermissionRequest.batchOffer; set once at request creation by the Host, never by callers; same additive pattern as resolution)
migrationsTable: existing migrations table gains 'ma2.approval-batches.v1' via INSERT OR IGNORE (same pattern as ma0.missions.v1; additive; no data rewriting)

stateMarker.issue: the installed-state marker (state-layout.json) records databaseSchemaSha256 at migration time; a Host applying its own additive schema at boot made every SECOND boot fail validation ("unexpected schema") with a healthy database — a restart of an activated T9 could never happen
stateMarker.change: refreshStateMarker (state-paths.server.ts): after the mission layer applies its schema, startHost reconciles the marker's databaseSchemaSha256 + databaseUserVersion to the APPLIED schema (read-only db read, marker fields rewritten, identity fields preserved; quick_check must pass or nothing is rewritten); non-installed state untouched
stateMarker.tests: src/lib/bunny-host/state-marker.test.ts (3): stale marker healed + second boot validates (defect reproduced first); current marker left byte-identical; damaged/wrong-version database refused and marker untouched
stateMarker.userVersion: PRAGMA user_version stays 3 the same as every prior gate; only the schema fingerprint moves

invariants: additive only: no existing column altered, no row rewritten, no data dropped
all Host databases (existing installations) upgrade on first boot with zero manual steps
the second boot after an additive migration validates and runs (renewed by the marker reconciliation)
the production database is never modified by the T9 development or staging flow; staging uses a disposable COPY
invariantsUpdated: the final invariant list replaces the earlier three-element list recorded with the pre-reconciliation tree
